points.event: >230,000 infected systems in >150 countries within the first 24 hours (Europol/Kaspersky)

threat.notes: extent = share of the ~230,000 systems reported infected in the first 24 h. Only endpoints are sourced; Kryptos Logic describes 'tens of thousands of infected systems per hour' at the peak (s3) but no sourced hourly series was found, so no doubling time is given. Sinkhole data (s3/MalwareTech) saw ~100,000 unique IPs in the first two days and >160,000 over May 12-15; MalwareTech warns the sinkhole graph is noisy. Most of the 24 h total accrued before the 7.3 h kill switch is plausible but NOT sourced; don't show a split.

aggregation.notes: Derived from documented response dates after t0, not a measured distribution: p10 = kill switch registered 7.3 h (s1), median ~ Microsoft's same-day emergency patch for unsupported systems (May 12 PT, ~20 h; hour unverified, s6), p90 = end of NHS disruption week May 19 (~168 h, s4). The deeper gap: the patch existed 1,416 h (59 days) before t0 and was not applied everywhere.

deploy.notes: NHS services affected for the week May 12-19, 2017.

ai_counterfactual.basis: Illustrative. Two steps: (1) reading a malware sample and spotting a hard-coded unregistered domain is a few-hour expert task (one researcher did it in ~7 h while also doing other work), inside the ~17.4 h 50% task horizon in RATES.md (METR entry); (2) matching an organisation's unpatched machines to a 59-day-old critical patch and routing the alert to the person who can apply it is inventory work that RATES.md's falling cost at fixed capability (~40x/year, Epoch) makes cheap to run continuously. Assumed ~1 h to the first working stop, and the patch fragment routed before t0. Humans still approve and apply patches. Not a claim the attack would certainly have been prevented.
ai_counterfactual.label: illustrative

gap_summary: The worm hit >150 countries within a day; the stop came at 7.3 h by one person's luck, the institutional fix took ~1 week to clear, and the patch had been sitting there for 59 days.
